Short answer: fully automated sending isn't something I'd build for you, but a fast semi-automated pipeline is very doable and honestly works better anyway. Here's the real picture.

**Why full auto-send is a bad idea, not just a technical hurdle**

- **WG-Gesucht's terms almost certainly prohibit scraping and automated/bot messaging** on the platform. Getting your account flagged or banned right when you need it most (starting now, for a September 1 move) is a real risk, not a theoretical one.
- **Auto-fired messages defeat the entire strategy in your own research.** Every source you've gathered agrees on one thing: personalization to the specific ad is the single biggest lever, and generic/templated-feeling messages get filtered out immediately. A script that fires the moment a listing appears has no way to judge fit (Frauen-WG, wrong dates, Zweckwohnung vibe, a hidden keyword test) or pull a genuinely specific detail — so you'd be sending fast, wrong messages instead of fast, right ones.
- **Speed still matters, but reading takes 20 seconds.** The advantage of being first doesn't require zero human involvement, just low friction.

**What I'd actually build instead: a fast human-in-the-loop pipeline**

1. **Alerts**: WG-Gesucht's own saved search (Suchaufträge) with push/email notifications, set as narrow as possible per neighborhood so you get pinged within minutes of a new listing.
2. **One-tap drafting**: the moment you get a notification, you open the listing, copy the ad text, paste it into this chat (or a Claude Project set up with your profile). I generate the German + English message in seconds using the system we've already built.
3. **You skim and send**: 30 seconds to check the fit note and personalization line, then paste into WG-Gesucht and hit send yourself.

If you want, I can also help you set up a simple **tracker** (a spreadsheet or artifact) to log every listing you apply to, response times, and outcomes, so you can see what's actually converting after ~15-20 applications. Want me to build that next?

Yes, this is buildable and you can have it running in about 30 minutes. The honest constraint: the sending stays manual, because that's what keeps you out of trouble with WG-Gesucht and it's only about 15 seconds of the loop anyway. Everything before the send can be made near-instant.

Target: **under 90 seconds from notification to sent message.**

**The loop, once it's set up:**

Notification hits. Open the listing, **screenshot it** (2–3 shots is fine, no copying or typing needed). Open Claude, new chat in the project, attach the screenshots, hit send with no message at all. You get back a one-line GO/SKIP verdict, the ad summarised in English, and the German message in a code block with a copy button. Skim the verdict, tap copy, paste into WG-Gesucht, send.

Two things matter more than drafting speed. First, **the SKIP verdict saves you the most time** — half of what lands in your alerts will be Frauen-WGs, short sublets, or wrong dates, and killing those in five seconds is worth more than a perfect draft. Second, **use a fresh chat per listing.** A long chat gets slower and starts bleeding details from the previous ad into the new one.

The screenshot-instead-of-copy trick is really the unlock here, and it only works on the phone:

Here's the file. Fill in Section 0 first, then upload it and paste it into project instructions.

Once you've done a dry run, send me the output and I'll tune whatever reads wrong.

dialogue.text:
Three separate things here. Let me be straight about which are real.

**The one thing I can't do: auto-fetch listings.** I only run when you message me, so there's no background process watching either site. I also can't reliably pull WG-Gesucht or Kleinanzeigen pages directly — both sit behind login walls and bot protection, and scraping them would put your account at risk. The sites' own push alerts are faster than anything I could poll anyway. Your screenshot stays the input.

**Kleinanzeigen is now built into the rules**, and it needed its own branch because it behaves differently: mostly landlords rather than flatmates, so Sie by default; shorter messages, 70–110 words, leading with BEGO income rather than your studio-to-WG story; and two or three missing facts asked directly, since those ads routinely omit the warm rent, whether Anmeldung is possible, or the minimum duration. Scam density there is much higher, so the SKIP triggers are more aggressive. Also watch that many hits are whole flats, not rooms.

**Furnishing is now a tracked field.** Möbliert and teilmöbliert show in the verdict as a plus. An empty room isn't a skip, because in Germany you normally ask about **Möbelübernahme** from the outgoing tenant, so that question gets built into the message automatically. If an **Ablöse** is named, that figure lands in the verdict since it's real money on top of your deposit.

**The full loop, end to end:**

Alert fires → open listing → screenshot → new chat in this project → attach, send blank. You get a source line, the verdict, English bullets, and the German block. Copy, paste, send on the site. Then paste the listing URL into the tracker and add it, which takes about fifteen seconds.

The tracker is where your "have I done this one" question gets answered. Paste a URL and it warns you if it's already logged, so you never double-apply. Anything sitting at "waiting" for three days surfaces in **Follow up today** at the top, which is your cue for the single follow-up in §8 of the rules. Data saves on the device you open it on, so use it from one place, ideally your phone.

Work newest-first and don't try to clear a backlog. A listing more than about two days old has usually already picked someone.

**Direct fetching is dead.** WG-Gesucht bounced me to a captcha page: it says bots are used to make abusive automatic submissions, so the site asks you to tick a checkbox and submit to prove you're a real human before continuing. The freshest listings are precisely the ones not indexed yet, and those are the only ones you can still win. So a sweep is a **backfill tool**, useful for catching older ads still sitting live, useless for the first-hour advantage.

So: I can do a sweep when you ask, and it'll give you candidate titles and links to open yourself. Just don't build your day around it.

**The real scale answer is batch mode, which I've now added to the rules.** Open the newest-first list (both sites default to newest at the top), screenshot four to six ads in one pass without opening each one, dump them all into a single message. dialogue.text:
Good challenge. Let me actually research the full space rather than repeat myself.

No Gmail tools on this connector set — worth knowing, since that closes one path and opens another. Let me research the wider landscape.

I dug into this properly. Here's the honest map of the entire space, including the parts I won't build for you.

**Full auto-send does exist.** There's a public GitHub project, `jonasdieker/wg-gesucht-bot`, that logs into your WG-Gesucht account with Playwright and sends messages to new listings, with an option to use a GPT model for more personalised messages. So I'm not telling you it's impossible. I'm telling you it's a bad trade, for one specific reason: it optimises the only variable that doesn't decide anything. Being message #3 instead of #30 helps. Being message #3 that reads like a template loses to message #30 that mentions Julian's football team. And if the account gets flagged three weeks before your move-in date, you have no channel at all. I won't help build it.

**The legitimate automation path is your own inbox, not the sites.** Alert emails belong to you, so processing them isn't scraping. Zapier, Make, n8n or a Google Apps Script can watch a Gmail label, call the Claude API, and push a result to Telegram. I checked whether I could read your Gmail directly from this chat, and I can't — those tools aren't on your connector set. But the real limit is different: WG-Gesucht alert emails carry the title, price, district and a link, not the ad body. So automation can do **triage, dedup and notification** genuinely well, and **drafting** genuinely badly. That's several hours of building for a three-week search. Worth it only if you'd enjoy building it.

**Claude in Chrome** is the closest legitimate version of what you actually asked for. It's a browsing agent that works inside your own logged-in browser under your supervision, so it can open your saved search and read listings without any scraping infrastructure. Still supervised, still you pressing send.

**Now the part I think actually matters.** You've been trying to automate one channel. The bigger win is that you're only fishing in one or two ponds.

**meinestadt.de** lists 327 WG rooms in Bremen and has free email Suchaufträge. Almost nobody applying on WG-Gesucht bothers with it. **Schwarzes Brett on bremen.de** carries free apartments from both private and commercial landlords, with WGs also advertising rooms there, plus a section where you can post your own request so landlords come to you. There's a Facebook page, "WG Zimmer frei in Bremen," with about 2,600 followers, plus the `bremen.immo` group. Facebook group notifications are push alerts, free, already built.

Two Bremen-specific programmes worth ten minutes each. **Study Friends** gives students rent-free WG rooms in exchange for educational support at primary and secondary schools, and it's been running about five years. Don't bother with Wohnen für Hilfe — it was discontinued last summer for lack of suitable housing offers. And **Studierendenwerk Bremen** runs 12 complexes with roughly 2,166 places, usually furnished and cheaper than the open market, though the waiting list averages around 250 students. Apply anyway as a backstop.

The one you're most likely to skip and shouldn't: **BEGO**. You work there. An internal noticeboard post or a word to colleagues reaches people with zero competition, and a Bremen employer vouching for a working student is worth more than any message I can write.

**And the inversion.** WG-Gesucht currently shows 114 people searching for a room in Bremen, and most of their Gesuche are lazy. Yours has real differentiators: steady BEGO income, long-term, definite September date. A strong Gesuch posted on WG-Gesucht, meinestadt, Schwarzes Brett and the Facebook groups is the only thing in this entire list that genuinely works while you sleep, and it's completely legitimate.

If I were ranking by payoff per hour: multi-channel alerts first, Gesuch everywhere second, BEGO and uni network third, batch mode in chat fourth. The email automation is sixth. The bot is last, and off the list.

Want me to write the Gesuch text for all four platforms? That's the highest-leverage thing left, and it's about fifteen minutes of work.
